claim: For a spherically symmetric heliosphere with a separable diffusion coefficient and negligible streaming, J(r, E, t) / (E^2 - E_0^2) = J(infinity, E + Phi) / ((E + Phi)^2 - E_0^2), with E the total energy, E_0 the rest energy and, for kappa_2 proportional to rigidity, Phi = |Z| e phi(r, t).

scope.text: force-field approximation; steady state; spherical symmetry

limitations: restated from the repository record of 2026-10-13; the zero-streaming equation is written in this profile's own notation (derive.py), not copied equation by equation

claim: phi is a single parameter describing the modulation and has the units of a potential (a fitted shift of -80 MV is quoted; Fig. 2 abscissa in BV).
limitations: restated from the repository record of 2026-10-13

claim: The force-field approximation breaks down below about 300 MeV per nucleon for protons and 250 MeV per nucleon for alpha particles, where streaming is no longer negligible.

scope.text: protons and alpha particles; other species not stated

limitations: approximate thresholds as stated by the authors for their model; not a sharp boundary

claim: Per nucleon, E^TOA / A = E^IS / A - (|Z| / A) phi and J^TOA(E^TOA) = (p^TOA / p^IS)^2 J^IS(E^IS), with J the flux per kinetic energy per nucleon and phi of the dimension of rigidity.

scope.text: force field in kinetic energy per nucleon

limitations: restated from the repository record of 2026-10-13

claim: The force field does not allow for any rigidity dependent effects and cannot predict the time dependence of the potential; studies often use different phi for positive and negative charges to allow charge-sign effects; phi is degenerate with injection and transport parameters.
limitations: restated from the repository record of 2026-10-13; the drift and charge-sign models themselves were not read
